RPGME TEST RUN, GAME 5, 18 NOVEMBER 2026

One couple, nine paths the first four games never took

Robin made a game on her phone for Sam, her fiancé(e). Sam is nonbinary and uses they/them. Our test buyer could now see the look pictures, so it picked looks by sight instead of taking the first one.

WHAT WE TESTED, AND WHAT HAPPENED

Five paths worked. Two broke, and two worked with problems.

BROKENA partner who uses they/themThe chat switched Sam to "she" because the best friend is a "she". Our buyer had to fix it by hand.
BROKENNo pet, so a favorite animalThe whole sentence was saved as the animal, and the red panda was called "the cat".
WORKED, WRONG WORDSThe couple photo described in wordsThe picture was made, but the chat said "Couldn't conjure the photo".
WORKED, EXTRA STEPS"None of these, try again" on looksIt asks what to change first. The four new looks were all the same.
WORKEDChange an answerThe song changed to "Landslide" and stayed changed. The button was not always on screen.
WORKEDLooks picked by sightRobin got a red hoodie and Sam a green sweater. No undressed looks.
WORKEDPhotos where both people look downThe site accepted both. Neither person looks at the camera.
WORKEDFiancé(e) and a typed occasionBoth saved word for word. The engagement got only "Noted!".
WORKED"No special keepsake"Saved as "They do not have a special keepsake".
BROKENTurns 47 to 49

The chat switched Sam from "they" to "she" on its own

Robin chose "they" for Sam early in the interview. Later she described the best friend: "Marisol! She's a pastry chef…". The chat answered "Got it, I'll use she/her for Sam from now on", and the next question asked about the joke that "always gets her".

It even rewrote Robin's earlier "They" answer to "She". A buyer who reads fast would not notice, and the game would call Sam "she".

A better way: change a pronoun only when the buyer answers the pronoun question about that person. Never read a pronoun from an answer about someone else.

BROKENTurns 49 to 54

The way to fix it was hidden

Our buyer typed "Sam uses they/them, not she/her" into its next answer. The chat offered "Change their name to Sam", which does not fix a pronoun.

Our buyer then tapped the old "She" answer higher up in the chat. Only then did the chat ask "Should I call Sam he, she or they?", and it went back to they/them.

A better way: when a buyer writes a pronoun correction, offer "Use they/them for Sam" as the button.

BROKENTurns 35 to 37

The favorite animal was saved as a whole sentence, then called a cat

With no pet, the chat asks for the partner's favorite animal, which becomes the sidekick. Robin answered "Red pandas! Sam has a whole sticky note collection of them mixed in with the cats."

The chat pasted that whole sentence, in lower case, into its next question, and then said "Juniper is a lovely name to use for the cat". The saved order shows the damage:

pet.name = Juniper
pet.type = "Red pandas! Sam has a whole sticky note collection of them mixed in with the cats"
pet.uniqueTrait = "always knows the way home" (nobody said this)

A better way: pull out the animal ("red panda") from the answer and confirm it with a button.

WRONG WORDSTurns 18 to 20

The chat said the couple picture failed, but it was made

Robin described the photo instead of uploading one: the ferry at sunset, right after she proposed, with Sam in her yellow raincoat. After 82 seconds, the chat said "Couldn't conjure the photo" and offered no retry. Then, in the next line, it said "Ha! I can already picture that scene".

The first try failed on the server (a 502 error), but a later try worked. The saved order holds the picture on the right.

A better way: show the picture when it arrives, and say "it failed" only when no picture will come.

REBUILT FROM THE PAGE TEXT
GAME MASTER
Couldn't conjure the photo. We can use your description for the story instead.
GAME MASTER
Ha! I can already picture that scene.
EXTRA STEPSTurns 21 to 28

"Try again" on looks asks what to change, then gives four of the same

Our buyer tapped "None of these, try again" on Sam's first looks. The chat asked what to change, and the buyer asked for the undercut, the nose ring and the hoops. The new looks took about two minutes, with no progress bar.

Our buyer reported that all four new looks were the same picture, with no nose ring. The chat then called the undercut "that stylish mohawk".

A better way: make four different looks on a redo, and show a short "drawing new looks" line while they are made.

WORKEDTurns 39 to 41

Changing an old answer works, once you find it

Our buyer changed Sam's song from "Dreams" to "Landslide" after the inside joke question. The chat asked what to save instead, said "I've updated that earlier answer", and went back to the next question. The saved order has "Landslide by Fleetwood Mac".

The "Change an answer" button showed at some moments, but not at this one. Our buyer had to guess that it could tap its old answer in the chat.

A better way: keep "Change an answer" on screen at every question.

WORKEDTurns 2 to 28

Real-life photos were accepted, and dressed looks were picked

Both photos are crops of one candid picture. Neither person looks at the camera, and the site accepted both.

This time our buyer saw the look pictures. It chose Robin's red hoodie look because of her curls and glasses. Sam's saved look is a green sweater, hoops and a nose ring. In the first four games, our buyer took the first look blindly, and that is how Grace and Hannah ended up with no visible clothes.

SMALLERTurns 13 to 18, 51, and the build

Small things that add up

The engagement got "Noted!" Big news, typed in by hand, got the same flat reply as the graduation in the best-friends game.

"Describe a moment" seems to do nothing. After the tap, the screen looks exactly the same, so the buyer cannot tell where to type.

The friend's job was asked twice again, and the villain service timed out once (a 524 error) during the build.

Robin tapped Build It! at 10:09 PM. "Your game is in!" showed 4 minutes later, and the build reached 80% by 10:33 PM. That is the point where the first four games were held for an hour because of billing. When the game finishes, these four checks run on the finished game.

WHERE TO START

Fix these three first, because each one can put wrong facts into a gift

Pronouns stay putOnly the pronoun question about a person may change that person's pronoun. Show a clear fix button.
Read the animal out of the answerSave "red panda", not the sentence, and never invent a habit.
Say what really happenedShow the couple picture when it arrives instead of "Couldn't conjure the photo".
